q: How do I calculate the cradle-to-gate carbon footprint of a submersible pump for an export buyer?
title: Submersible pump footprint per unit
short: Weigh each material in the pump's bill of materials, as bought including scrap, and multiply by its emission factor: copper winding, stainless steel, cast iron, electrical steel, plastics and cable. Then add your factory's fuel and electricity per pump. Materials usually make up most of a cradle to gate figure; use phase is reported separately.
audience: Coimbatore and Rajkot pump and motor makers

sections.h: What cradle to gate covers for a pump
p: Cradle to gate stops when the packed pump leaves your factory. It covers raw materials, bought-in parts, their transport to you, your own fuel and electricity, packaging and production waste. The electricity the pump uses over its life is a separate figure, Scope 3 Category 11 for your inventory, and should not be added into the product footprint you quote per unit.

sections.h: Build it from the bill of materials
ol: List every material by mass for one model: copper winding wire, stainless steel shaft and impellers, cast iron bowls or motor body, electrical steel laminations, plastics such as impellers or diffusers, cable if it ships with the pump.
Use mass bought, not mass in the product. Machining chips and stamping skeletons from laminations are part of the input.

Take factors from your suppliers first, such as a wire maker's or steel mill's product figure. Otherwise use a named published dataset for copper cathode, stainless or electrical steel, and state its year.
Bought-in parts such as bearings, capacitors or control panels: use supplier figures, or estimate by material mass and say so.

p: Take a month's electricity and fuel, multiply by their factors (0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25 for grid power, 2.68 kg CO2 per litre of diesel), and divide by pumps made. If you make 0.5 HP and 10 HP models on the same lines, divide by kg of pump produced or by machine hours instead, so the big models carry more. Include winding, varnish curing ovens, machining and the test tank.

sections.h: What an export buyer will check
ul: The functional unit, such as one pump of a stated model and rating.
The source and year of each material factor.
How factory energy was divided between models.
Whether cable, packaging and the control panel are in or out.

example.title: Illustrative example: an 18 kg submersible pump set
lines: Copper winding 2.0 kg x 4.0 = 8.0 kg CO2e
Stainless steel 4.0 kg x 6.0 = 24.0 kg CO2e
Cast iron 6.0 kg x 1.5 = 9.0 kg CO2e
Electrical steel 5.0 kg x 2.5 = 12.5 kg CO2e
Plastics 1.0 kg x 3.0 = 3.0 kg CO2e; materials total 56.5 kg CO2e
Factory: 60,000 kWh for 4,000 pumps = 15 kWh, x 0.710 = 10.65 kg CO2
DG diesel: 800 litres for 4,000 pumps = 0.2 litre, x 2.68 = 0.536 kg CO2
example.note: Material factors here are placeholders in kg CO2e per kg, chosen only to show the arithmetic. Replace each with a supplier or named dataset figure before sending to a buyer.

senseible: Senseible reads your factory's electricity, diesel and other fuel bills into Scope 1 and 2 totals, which you divide across pumps. Material factors come from your suppliers or published datasets.
